NEW DELHI: The Election Commission on Friday told the Supreme Court that over 37 lakh appeals against the deletion or inclusion of names in West Bengal electoral rolls under the Special Intensive Revision remain pending.The poll panel told the apex court in its response affidavit that tribunals appointed by the court have disposed of only about 1.02 lakh of the 38.20 lakh appeals filed so far.This comes after a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymala Bagchi and V Mohana sought the poll panel's response to a plea seeking disclosure of assembly constituency-wise data on claims and objections filed by voters whose names were deleted during the SIR exercise.A total of 38,20,683 appeals had been filed against orders relating to the SIR of electoral rolls. Of these, 1,02,231 appeals had been disposed of, leaving 37,18,452 pending, the poll panel said.The affidavit, however, did not provide a break-up of the appeals filed by electors whose names were deleted and those filed against the inclusion of names in the electoral rolls.Prasenjit Bose, who filed the affidavit, claimed that more than 58 lakh electors were excluded during the enumeration phase of the SIR exercise in West Bengal.
He added that while 9.64 lakh applications for inclusion (Forms 6 and 6A) and over 99,000 applications for deletion (Form 7) were received during the claims and objections phase, only around 1.82 lakh additions were reflected in the final electoral roll published on February 28.On August 25, the top court directed the Election Commission to submit data on the pendency and disposal of appeals before tribunals challenging exclusion or inclusion in electoral rolls.Observing that these appeals needed to be adjudicated in a time-bound manner, the bench had asked the poll panel to explain what steps were being taken to streamline the mechanism for disposing of pending appeals and how many additional tribunals were required.
The EC data submitted to the court showed that 34.13 lakh Form 6 applications had been filed between December 17, 2025, when the draft electoral roll was published, and August 7, 2026.Form 6 is the statutory application for inclusion of a name in the electoral roll.On April 24, the apex court asked the appellate tribunals to give out-of-turn hearings to those who made a case for urgent hearing against deletion from electoral rolls after the SIR.Approximately 700 judicial officers from West Bengal and neighbouring Odisha and Jharkhand were deployed to deal with around 60 lakh claims and objections.Later, the chief justice of the Calcutta high court, on the direction of the top court, set up 19 tribunals headed by former high court chief justices and judges to decide the appeals.

FSSAI said it examined the products and their promotional material available on e-commerce platforms.
The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) on Friday initiated legal action against Nestle India over alleged non-compliance involving its NAN Excella Pro Stage 1 and Lactogen Pro 1 infant nutrition products.FSSAI said it examined the products and their promotional material available on e-commerce platforms. In the case of NAN Excella Pro Stage 1, the regulator flagged claims relating to “5 HMOs” and “Whey Protein”. For Lactogen Pro 1, it raised concerns over a claim that the product’s “Whey Protein” was easy to digest.According to FSSAI, both products were found to be in contravention of Regulation 4(2) of the Food Safety and Standards (Foods for Infant Nutrition) Regulations, 2020. The provision restricts promotional claims and material intended to increase the saleability of infant foods. The regulator also cited Section 3 of the Infant Milk Substitutes, Feeding Bottles and Infant Foods (Regulation of Production, Supply and Distribution) Act, 1992, which prohibits their advertisement and promotion.
FSSAI said it had sought clarifications from Nestle India regarding the claims.Separately, a sample of a follow-up formula manufactured by Nestle India was found to be sub-standard for its biotin content during laboratory analysis.
The sample was sent for re-analysis, but the referral laboratory also found it non-conforming with the prescribed biotin requirement under the 2020 regulations.In view of the alleged violations, FSSAI said three separate adjudication cases have been filed against Nestle India in relation to the products. The action covers both promotional claims and the laboratory finding concerning biotin content.

Russia begins 3-day legislative elections as Kremlin seeks to project support for war
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-18
07:47:51 UTC
16:47:51 KST

Russia begins 3-day legislative elections as Kremlin seeks to project support for war
Russia on Sept. 18 began its three-day elections for the 450-member State Duma, the lower chamber of Russia's legislature, for the first time since the outbreak of the full-scale war in Ukraine.
Russian voters will also go to the polls to cast their ballots for 11 regional governors and 39 regional parliaments.
Elections in Russia are tightly controlled by the regime but can help the Kremlin gauge the level of public support for the invasion of Ukraine, now ongoing for more than four and a half years.
The ruling United Russia party, backed by Russian President Vladimir Putin, is broadly expected to maintain control over the Russian legislature.
Other parties permitted to run, such as the Communist Party or the ultranationalist Liberal Democratic Party (LDPR), are part of the so-called "systemic opposition," a group of Kremlin-aligned parties meant to create the appearance of democratic competition.
Yabloko, Russia's only anti-war party, was barred from running in August, while other "non-systemic opposition" politicians in Russia have been persecuted, forced into exile, or killed.
Speaking days before the elections, Putin framed the vote as a chance for the Russian people to demonstrate their support for the war in Ukraine.
"Your choice and your will will once again demonstrate that millions of people stand behind our troops, that we are a single people, united by common values, historical memory and love for the Motherland," the Russian leader said in an address on Sept. 16.
Democracy watchdogs regard the Russian elections as neither free nor fair, and independent Russian media have already reported intimidation of election observers and coercion of voters in the run-up to the vote.
The last State Duma elections took place in 2021, a few months before Russia launched its full-scale invasion in Ukraine. This year will mark the first time that Moscow will illegally hold elections for the State Duma also in the Ukrainian territories occupied after 2022.

Geran drones destroy Ukrainian radar stations, electronic warfare system

Unknown Publisher
2026-09-18
07:43:35 UTC
16:43:35 KST

MOSCOW, September 18. /TASS/. Russian Geran-4 drone crews have destroyed radar stations and an electronic warfare system used by the Ukrainian army in the Dnepropetrovsk and Odessa Regions, Russia’s Defense Ministry said in a statement.
"Moving vehicles of the 79K6 Pelikan radar station were detected near the settlement of Dalnik in the Odessa Region. The vehicles were tracked, and a Geran-4 drone operator carried out a strike when the radar began to deploy," the statement reads.
The ministry also said that a P-19MA radar station and a dome electronic warfare system had been destroyed near Shirokoye in the Dnepropetrovsk Region.

Russians’ level of trust in Putin exceeds 74% — pollster
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-18
07:41:16 UTC
16:41:16 KST

MOSCOW, September 28. /TASS/. The level of trust among Russians in President Vladimir Putin stands at 74.2%, according to a survey conducted by the Russian Public Opinion Research Center.
The study was conducted among 1,600 adult Russians from September 7 to 13.
"When asked about trust in Putin, a total of 74.2% of survey participants answered positively, with the level of approval for the president’s performance standing at 70.1%," the pollster noted.
The Russian government’s work is approved by 48.3% of respondents. Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin’s activities received approval from 46.2% of those surveyed, with 54.6% of survey participants expressing confidence in him.

Soyuz-2.1b rocket successfully places satellite into orbit — Defense Ministry
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-18
07:35:01 UTC
16:35:01 KST

MOSCOW, September 18. /TASS/. The launch of the Soyuz-2.1b carrier rocket with a spacecraft from the Plesetsk spaceport went according to plan, the Russian Defense Ministry reported.
"The launch of the carrier rocket and the placement of the spacecraft into its intended orbit proceeded as planned. After launch, the medium-class Soyuz-2.1b carrier rocket was tracked by the ground-based automated control system of the German Titov Main Test and Space Systems Control Center," the ministry said in a statement.
The spacecraft was put into its target orbit at the scheduled time and was placed under control of ground-based assets of the Aerospace Forces’ Space Troops, the ministry reported. "Stable telemetry communication with the spacecraft has been established and maintained, and its onboard systems are functioning normally," the ministry added.
